title: Testing with React Testing Library concepts
summary: Testing behaviour instead of implementation, render and screen, query priority, getBy versus queryBy versus findBy, user events, async updates, act and mocking.

sections.title: Test what the user sees
sections.body: React Testing Library (RTL) renders a component into a real DOM (usually jsdom) and asks you to interact with it the way a user would: find elements by **role and accessible name**, click and type, then assert on the visible result. Avoid testing implementation details such as state variable names, internal methods or component instances; those tests break on harmless refactors.

sections.title: Queries
sections.body:
Prefer queries in this order: `getByRole` (with `{ name }`), `getByLabelText`, `getByPlaceholderText`, `getByText`, `getByDisplayValue`, then `getByAltText` and `getByTitle`; `getByTestId` is the last resort.

- `getBy…` returns one element or **throws** if there are none or several.
- `queryBy…` returns the element or **null**; use it to assert something is **absent**.
- `findBy…` returns a **promise** that retries until the element appears (default 1 second); use it for async UI.
- `getAllBy…`, `queryAllBy…` and `findAllBy…` return arrays.
sections.code:
render(<Login />)
await user.type(screen.getByLabelText("Email"), "ada@example.com")
await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Sign in" }))
expect(await screen.findByText("Welcome, Ada")).toBeInTheDocument()
expect(screen.queryByRole("alert")).not.toBeInTheDocument()

sections.title: Events and async updates
sections.body:
`@testing-library/user-event` (`const user = userEvent.setup()`) simulates full interactions: `await user.click(el)`, `await user.type(el, "text")`, `await user.keyboard("{Enter}")`. It is closer to real behaviour than `fireEvent`, which dispatches a single event.

State updates after promises or timers happen later; wait for them with `findBy…` or `waitFor(() => expect(…))`. RTL wraps `render` and its events in `act`, so you rarely call `act` yourself; the warning "An update … was not wrapped in act(...)" usually means a test finished before an async update. Use fake timers (`vi.useFakeTimers()` or `jest.useFakeTimers()`) for timer logic.

sections.title: Mocks
sections.body: Pass dependencies in as props or context so tests can supply fakes, or mock modules (`vi.mock`, `jest.mock`). Use mock functions (`vi.fn()`, `jest.fn()`) for callbacks and assert `toHaveBeenCalledWith(...)`. For network calls, Mock Service Worker intercepts requests at the network layer. Restore mocks between tests.

pitfalls: `getBy…` for something that appears after a promise; use `findBy…`.
Selecting by class name or test id when a role and name would work.
Asserting on internal state instead of the rendered output.

gotchas.question: Which query returns `null` instead of throwing when nothing matches?
A message appears after a fetch resolves. Which query should you use?
gotchas.answer: `await screen.findByText(...)`, which retries until it appears or times out.

gotchas.question: Which query does RTL recommend first?
gotchas.answer: `getByRole`, usually with `{ name }`, because it matches how assistive technology finds elements.
